assessment.calibration_basis: p_engine=0.9456, cms_p=0.9573, cal_p=0.7784; the scorecard's adjustments show the customer-denial floor (0.55) raised by the corroboration factor (x1.1, since the calibrated score is >=0.5) and a further bump for the recent same-channel CNP case history (+0.5 on the log-odds scale). I set fraud_probability at 0.92, within p_engine +/-0.10, staying close to the engine because the fraud-family evidence (customer denial, cms_p 0.9573 on the flagged transaction, 18 prior confirmed-fraud closed cases on this exact card with the same CNP pattern, and a failed R7 recurring-charge gate) is corroborated and multi-family, while the legitimacy-family evidence (amount inside the card's baseline, device seen 9 times before) is the kind of signal the engine already folds into cal_p and does not on its own explain away an unresolved denial on a card with this fraud history.

evidence.claim: Customer C13171 denies making the $55.68 purchase 3558054 ('I never made this $55.68 purchase'); this denial is the case trigger and, per the bank's history, 0 of prior customer-reported denials were ever cleared.

The case-memory scorer places the flagged transaction 3558054 at cms_p=0.957266 (calibrated cal_p=0.7784), far above the real-time risk_score of 0.38, and the immediately preceding transaction 3557979 (21:48, $55.60) also scores 0.927636 on the same scorer.

card_profile lists 18 prior closed cases on this exact card (C13171-K2), all outcome confirmed_fraud, patterns card_not_present_new_device / card_not_present_fraud, most recently CC-5010 opened 2016-10-19; only one other closed case (CC-4819) was cleared as a new-phone false alarm.

recurring_charge_check on 3558054 found a hotmail.com group of 5 prior purchases within +-1% of the amount but with gap_cv=1.109554, well above the 0.6 ceiling the R7 exception requires, so this is not the customer's own regular recurring charge and R2 (block/case) governs rather than R7.

episode_candidates shows transactions 3557979 ($55.60, 21:48:32), 3557987 ($55.69, 21:50:54, device_new=New) and 3558054 ($55.68, 22:08:56) as a signature-matched cluster (sig_match=true) sharing the same device profile 'NULL | NULL | chrome 66.0 | NULL' and the same hotmail.com purchaser/recipient email within a 20-minute span, giving an exposure of $166.97 across the three; the New-device member 3557987 drives the card_not_present_new_device label.

card_testing_check over the 217-member online chain found only 2 sub-$5 members and no larger-purchase-after-run shape (larger_purchase amt=0), ruling out the R5 card-testing pattern for this episode.

device_history shows the device profile 'NULL | NULL | chrome 66.0 | NULL' was already used on this card 9 times before this episode, first seen 2016-12-05, so the profile itself is not novel to the card even though one member transaction (3557987) is individually flagged device_new=New.
The flagged amount $55.68 sits inside the card's pre-opening baseline (899 prior transactions, prior median $39.37, prior maximum $407.32), so amount alone would not have flagged this purchase.

actions.reason: 3a: fraud probability 0.92 exceeds the 0.30 case-opening threshold and the customer disputed transaction 3558054, so a case is opened to record the episode ($166.97 exposure across 3557979, 3557987, 3558054).
R2/§3b: the customer denied transaction 3558054 and the recurring-charge gate (R7) does not apply (gap_cv 1.11 > 0.6), so blocking is recommended; exposure $166.97 ≤ $2,500 keeps this at L1.
